Gauge covariance of the Schrödinger equation

Words: 26
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
For a particle of charge −e, the changes A↦A+∇f and ϕ↦ϕ−∂t​f leave the minimally coupled Schrödinger equation invariant when ψ↦e−ief/ℏψ.

Quantum measurement

Words: 289 Articles: 10
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum measurement assigns probabilities to classical outcomes through positive operators that sum to the identity. A projective measurement uses mutually orthogonal projections.

Measurement interaction

Words: 22
Quantum measurement OurBigBook.com
A measurement interaction correlates a measured system's alternatives with distinguishable states of an apparatus. Reading the apparatus then implements the associated quantum measurement.

Generalized measurement postulate

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Quantum measurement OurBigBook.com
A generalized quantum measurement is specified by operators Mi​ satisfying ∑i​Mi†​Mi​=I. On input ρ, outcome i has probability Tr(Mi†​Mi​ρ) and conditional state Mi​ρMi†​/Tr(Mi†​Mi​ρ).

Positive operator-valued measure (POVM)

Words: 30
Generalized measurement postulate OurBigBook.com
A positive operator-valued measure is a family of positive operators Ei​ satisfying ∑i​Ei​=I. It determines measurement probabilities Pr(i)=Tr(Ei​ρ); choosing measurement operators with Ei​=Mi†​Mi​ additionally determines state updates.

Projective measurement

Words: 89 Articles: 3
Quantum measurement OurBigBook.com
A projective measurement is specified by mutually orthogonal projections Pi​ with ∑i​Pi​=I. On a state ρ, outcome i has probability Tr(Pi​ρ).

Lüders rule

Words: 65 Articles: 2
Projective measurement OurBigBook.com
Conditional on outcome i of a projective measurement, the Lüders rule updates the state to
ρi​=Tr(Pi​ρ)Pi​ρPi​​.
(1)
Post-measurement state
Words: 22
Lüders rule OurBigBook.com
The post-measurement state is the conditional quantum state after a specified measurement outcome. For a projective measurement, it is given by the Lüders rule.
Nonselective projective measurement
Words: 27
Lüders rule OurBigBook.com
If the outcome of a projective measurement {Pi​} is discarded, its nonselective state update is the pinching channel
ρ⟼∑i​Pi​ρPi​.
(2)
It removes coherence between distinct measurement subspaces.

Quantum state tomography

Words: 28
Quantum measurement OurBigBook.com
Quantum state tomography estimates enough expectation values on many identically prepared systems to reconstruct their density operator. A single ordinary specimen cannot provide arbitrarily many independent samples without disturbance.

No information without disturbance

Words: 67 Articles: 1
Quantum measurement OurBigBook.com
If a quantum instrument leaves every input state unchanged even after conditioning on its classical output, then its output distribution is independent of the input state. Thus an ordinary quantum process cannot learn arbitrary state information while preserving every state.

Quantum instrument

Words: 29
No information without disturbance OurBigBook.com
A quantum instrument associates each classical outcome with a completely positive trace-nonincreasing map; summing the outcome maps gives a quantum channel. It specifies both outcome probabilities and conditional output states.

Amplitude amplification

Words: 156 Articles: 3
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
If a state has good amplitude sinθ, the product of the reflection in the bad axis and the reflection in the state line rotates its good-bad plane by 2θ. After k iterations the good probability is
sin2((2k+1)θ),
(3)
so O(1/sinθ) iterations raise a small good amplitude close to one.

Exact amplitude amplification

Words: 80 Articles: 1
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
If the initial good amplitude p=sinθ is known, an ancillary qubit can reduce it to sinθ′=pc with θ′=π/(4k+2) and 0<c≤1. After k ordinary amplitude-amplification iterations the good amplitude is sin((2k+1)θ′)=1, so the target state is prepared exactly.

Phase-matched amplitude amplification

Words: 40
Exact amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
Phase-matched amplitude amplification replaces the two sign-flip reflections by selective phase rotations. Choosing their phases from the known initial overlap can rotate the state exactly onto the target even when an integer number of ordinary Grover rotations would overshoot it.

Geometric amplitude-amplification schedule

Words: 26
Amplitude amplification OurBigBook.com
A geometric amplitude-amplification schedule tries iteration counts 1,2,4,8,… when the initial good amplitude is unknown. It reaches the unknown optimal scale with only a geometric-series overhead.

Reflection operator

Words: 83 Articles: 1
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
For a unit vector ∣ψ⟩, the reflection I−2∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣ negates the component parallel to ∣ψ⟩ and fixes its orthogonal complement.

Selective phase rotation

Words: 63
Reflection operator OurBigBook.com
For a unit vector ∣ψ⟩ and real ϕ,
Rψϕ​=I−(1−eiϕ)∣ψ⟩⟨ψ∣
(4)
multiplies the component parallel to ∣ψ⟩ by eiϕ and fixes its orthogonal complement. The case ϕ=π is a reflection operator.

Injective matrix product state (injective MPS)

Words: 325 Articles: 9
Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
An MPS tensor is injective after blocking when products of its physical matrices span the full virtual matrix algebra.
Blocking a matrix product state
Words: 39
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
Blocking L neighboring sites replaces their physical labels by one composite label and their tensor by the products Ai1​⋯AiL​. An MPS is injective when such products span the full virtual matrix algebra for some finite L.
Uniform matrix product state (uniform MPS)
Words: 24
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
A uniform matrix product state uses the same local tensor Ai at every site. For a periodic chain its amplitudes are Tr(Ai1​⋯AiN​).
Fundamental theorem of matrix product states (fundamental theorem of MPS)
Words: 62 Articles: 1
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
Two injective uniform MPS tensors generate the same states on every sufficiently long periodic chain exactly when they differ by a virtual similarity transform and an overall phase: Ai=eiθXBiX−1.
Gauge equivalence of injective matrix product state tensors
Words: 32
Fundamental theorem of matrix product states OurBigBook.com
The virtual similarity transformation Ai↦XAiX−1 leaves every periodic MPS amplitude invariant by cyclicity of the matrix trace. The fundamental theorem of matrix product states says that, up to an overall phase, this is the only ambiguity for injective uniform tensors.
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state (AKLT state)
Words: 181 Articles: 4
Injective matrix product state OurBigBook.com
The Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state is an injective spin-one MPS whose virtual degrees of freedom are spin one-half. Its Z2​×Z2​ symmetry acts linearly on physical spins and projectively on the virtual spins.
Pauli-matrix representation of the Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state
Words: 76 Articles: 1
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
In a Cartesian basis of the physical spin-one space, the AKLT MPS matrices are proportional to σx​,σy​,σz​. Products of two such matrices span the full virtual matrix algebra, and the two-site parent term projects onto total spin two.
Two-site support of the Pauli-matrix Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki tensor
Words: 37
Pauli-matrix representation of the Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
Because σi​σj​=δij​I+iεijk​σk​, the two-site image of the Pauli-matrix AKLT tensor is the direct sum of the scalar and antisymmetric subspaces, which have total spin zero and one. Its orthogonal complement is the symmetric traceless total-spin-two subspace.
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki parent Hamiltonian (AKLT parent Hamiltonian)
Words: 38
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
The AKLT parent Hamiltonian is H=∑j​Pj,j+1(2)​, where P(2) projects two neighboring spin-one particles onto total spin two. It is frustration free, and the periodic AKLT MPS is its unique ground state on a sufficiently long chain.
Symmetry-protected equivalence of the Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state and cluster state
Words: 35
Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki state OurBigBook.com
After suitable blocking, the AKLT and one-dimensional cluster states realize the same nontrivial Z2​×Z2​ symmetry-protected topological phase. Their virtual symmetries carry the same nontrivial projective class and produce protected edge degrees of freedom.

Entanglement spectrum of a matrix product state

Words: 28
Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
The entanglement spectrum is the spectrum of −logρA​, equivalently the negative logarithms of squared Schmidt coefficients. A nontrivial projective virtual symmetry can enforce degeneracies throughout this spectrum.

Parent Hamiltonian of a matrix product state (MPS parent Hamiltonian)

Words: 26
Matrix product state OurBigBook.com
An MPS parent Hamiltonian is a sum of local projectors onto the orthogonal complement of the tensor's local support. The MPS is a frustration-free ground state.

A matrix product operator contracts a one-dimensional chain of tensors with physical input and output indices.

Projected entangled pair state (PEPS)

Tensor network state OurBigBook.com
A projected entangled pair state generalizes an MPS to higher-dimensional lattices. Cutting a region intersects one virtual bond per boundary edge.

Projected entangled pair operator (PEPO)

Words: 16
Tensor network state OurBigBook.com
A projected entangled pair operator is a higher-dimensional tensor-network operator with physical input and output legs.

Hamiltonian simulation

Words: 220 Articles: 7
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
Hamiltonian simulation constructs a quantum circuit approximating the time-evolution operator e−itH generated by a Hamiltonian operator H, with cost controlled by the evolution time, requested precision, and structure of H.

Commuting local Hamiltonian simulation

Words: 29
Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
If H=∑j​hj​ and all local terms commute, then
e−itH=∏j​e−ithj​
(115)
exactly. Approximating each fixed-size factor to error at most ε/m and applying the telescoping bound for products of operators gives total operator norm error at most ε.

Local Hamiltonian

Words: 119 Articles: 3
Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
A local Hamiltonian is a sum of terms, each acting nontrivially on only a bounded number of subsystems.

Diagonal Hamiltonian

Words: 35
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A diagonal Hamiltonian is diagonal in a specified product basis, usually the computational basis. Every basis state is therefore an energy eigenstate, and optimization of its diagonal entries becomes minimization of the corresponding classical cost function.

Frustration-free quantum Hamiltonian

Words: 38
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A quantum Hamiltonian H=∑j​hj​ with positive-semidefinite local terms is frustration free when one state minimizes every hj​ simultaneously. After shifting each local minimum to zero, that state lies in every kernel kerhj​ and has zero total energy.

k-local Hamiltonian (k-local Hamiltonian)

Words: 28
Local Hamiltonian OurBigBook.com
A k-local Hamiltonian is a sum of terms that each act nontrivially on at most k subsystems. The integer k remains fixed as the system size grows.

Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation

Words: 44 Articles: 1
Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation approximates e−it(A+B) by alternating exponentials of A and B, which are assumed easier to implement separately.

Second-order product formula

Words: 24
Product-formula Hamiltonian simulation OurBigBook.com
The symmetric second-order formula, also called Strang splitting, is
e−iδA/2e−iδBe−iδA/2=e−iδ(A+B)+O(δ3)
(116)
for bounded operators, with the constant controlled by nested commutators.

Block encoding

Words: 36
Quantum theory OurBigBook.com
A block encoding of a matrix A is a unitary operator whose designated block equals A/α for a known normalization factor α. It gives a quantum circuit coherent access to matrices that need not themselves be unitary.
